Causeway Approach Mandeville, LA 70471 RE: Katherine Moller o/b/o Harmony Moller (D) v Martian Sales, Inc., et al; US District Court, Eastern District of Louisiana; Civil Action NO. 24-0228-WBV-DPC Dear Mr. Wagar: I am a physician certified in cardiovascular disease by the American Board of Internal Medicine. I received my medical degree from the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Columbia University in 1989. I completed a residency in Internal Medicine at Montefiore Medical Center in Bronx, NY, followed by a fellowship in cardiovascular disease at Maimonides Medical Center in Brooklyn, NY. I am currently an Associate Professor of Cardiology at the Zucker School of Medicine of Hofstra University, NY, and an attending cardiologist at North Shore University Hospital, Manhasset, NY. You contacted me on September 16, 2025, and requested whether I would be interested in reviewing certain medical and other documents regarding the captioned case pending in the federal court in New Orleans involving the sudden death of Harmony Moller on February 6, 2023, at her home. Upon assenting, you provided me with certain documents which I reviewed and, pertinent to this inquiry, included: • Images of the front and back of packages of Green Vein Maeng Da Kratom powder and of Maeng Da Kratom capsules by OPMS that were found in the bedroom of the decedent at the time of her death; • A copy of the Certificate of Death of Harmony Moller by Charles Allen Preston, Coroner; • Postmortem Forensic Medical Examination Report, St. Tammany Parish Coroner’s Office consisting of four pages; • Attached Toxicology Report by NMS Labs regarding the decedent and dated February 24, 2023 consisting of five pages; • Sample Analysis Report by Clinical Toxicology and Environmental Biomonitoring Laboratory dated April 18, 2023, consisting of one page and signed by Ross Ellison and Roy Gerona, Ph.D; and • Jesse E. Edwards Registry of Cardiovascular Disease heart pathology report consisting of four pages and signed by Shannon M. Mackey- Bojack, MD.

Case 2:24-cv-00228-WBV-DPC Document 267-58 Filed 03/02/26 Page 3 of 12 Specifically, you requested my opinion as to the cause of the sudden death of Harmony Moller. It is my opinion that Harmony Moller, an otherwise healthy 36-year-old young woman, suffered a cardiorespiratory cause of death on February 6, 2023. Pertinent Medical History: It is my understanding that the decedent was found on autopsy to have what was described as “abnormally high left coronary ostia takeoff exacerbated by mitragynine use”. It is also my understanding that Harmony Moller had no prodrome prior to her being found pulseless by her mother in the early morning hours. She had no recent medical illness and no chronic medical conditions, as was confirmed at autopsy. I have also been asked to assume that Harmony Moller had resided in Southeast Asia as a teacher for some thirteen years, returning to the United States in 2021 to help care for her ailing father prior to his death. Apparently, while there, Harmony Moller had consumed natural Mitragyna speciosa leaf and, upon returning, purchased and consumed kratom sold in local stores in the area where she lived in Louisiana. The toxicology report confirmed the presence of mitragynine (150 ng/mL) in her femoral blood. Discussion: There are multiple reports in the medical literature that associate the use of kratom products with the development of ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation (VT/VF), which cause the heart to stop beating. This leads to the immediate cessation of circulation and death within a few minutes unless treated with defibrillation. My opinion is based on exclusion, as a cardiorespiratory death, such as cardiac arrhythmia, cannot be confirmed by autopsy or postmortem toxicology. Sudden death occurs from either an anatomic or a toxic/metabolic cause. No anatomic cause (traumatic, cardiac, thromboembolic, or neurologic) was identified. There is no medical history of any condition that would cause a dangerous metabolic derangement (there were no chronic medical conditions identified at autopsy), nor was there any family history of premature sudden cardiac death. Cardiac adverse events such as VT/VF can be precipitated by exogenous substances. A comprehensive review of opioid-associated arrhythmia in North America published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology in 2023 by Krantz et. al.1 demonstrated a “disproportionate” association of “life threatening arrhythmias in North America” with mitragynine. While data and research into kratom is evolving, the literature discussing kratom consumption and its effects suggests a significant linkage between the main alkaloid in 2

Case 2:24-cv-00228-WBV-DPC Document 267-58 Filed 03/02/26 Page 4 of 12 Mitragyna speciosa (kratom) use, ventricular arrhythmias (ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation) and cardiorespiratory adverse events1,2. In March 2025, potentially fatal effects on the electrocardiogram attributed to the use of kratom were published3,4. Conclusions: 1. Harmony Moller had no known signs or symptoms of chronic or acute disease or injury presaging her sudden death prior to her demise on February 6, 2023. 2. The high ostia take-off of the left coronary artery is a benign finding which was not a cause of her sudden death. 3. In my opinion, more likely than not, Harmony Moller died from a cardiorespiratory adverse event induced by consumption of kratom. The conclusions reached in this report are based on my education, training, and experience, and are all within reasonable medical probability. This report is based on the material I have been asked to review as of November 4, 2025. I am being compensated at a rate of $700/hr for my consultation in this case. I reserve the right to amend this report should further information become available. Ronald H. Wharton MD, FACC, FASE References: 1. Krantz, M.J. et. al.
